but both are statistically insignificant as of the first quarter of 2026. yale budget lab: 16-34 cohort unemployment ~+0.5pp but statistically insignificant we also examine the log real hourly wages of ai-exposed and unexposed workers... we see no statistically or economically significant impact through 2026q1. yale budget lab: no statistically significant ai wage effect through 2026q1 (sdid)
noahpinion-ai-messaging-pivot-2026: ai's big messaging pivot noahpinion (noah smith) major ai industry figures (altman, jensen huang, andreessen) are pivoting from displacement-focused messaging to augmentation-focused messaging amid deteriorating public opinion on ai. the new pitch: ai will create new tasks in the short term (task creation, jevons paradox), and in the long term humans will be paid for the 'relational sector' where the human element is the product itself. noah smith cautiously endorses the new pitch as better pr and potentially self-fulfilling for research direction, while noting it may be partly competitive positioning by openai against anthropic.
